construction.anchor_treatments: two levels alternating by column, both with f(d)=1

proof_obligations.algorithm_estimate: Conditional on each observed S, its leading singular vectors are independent of q and x. Their two inner products are O_p(1), while s_1(S)>=||S||_F/sqrt(N)=Omega_p(sqrt(N)); hence each exact rank-one PCR estimate is O_p(N^-1/2), up to an immaterial logarithm uniformly over polynomial K.
proof_obligations.anchor_construction: Algorithm 3 incidence matrix B is all ones on KN rows by N columns. Its full matrix is a maximum biclique; its rows admit K disjoint size-N partitions and its columns alternate two treatments.
proof_obligations.assumption_2_1: For both treatments, Y_ij^(d)=u_i v_j^(d)+epsilon_ij^(d) is an exact rank-one factorization.
proof_obligations.assumption_2_2: The treatment design is deterministic and every noise entry is independent and mean-zero conditional on U, V, and D.
proof_obligations.assumption_2_4: Every scalar row factor is nonzero, so any nonempty donor set spans every scalar target factor; mu=1 is universal.
proof_obligations.assumption_2_5: The same scalar row factor is used for both treatments.
proof_obligations.assumption_4_1: All latent row and column factors have magnitude at most one, so all expected potential outcomes lie in [-1,1].
proof_obligations.assumption_4_2: Independent fixed-variance Gaussian noise is mean-zero sub-Gaussian with a universal norm constant.
proof_obligations.assumption_4_3: Rank is one, so tau_r/tau_1=1, and the stated upper bound holds with a universal constant although tau_1 vanishes.
proof_obligations.assumption_4_4: E[x]=u_N is exactly in Col(E[S_w])=span(u_N), even though Theorem 4.5 omits Assumption 4.4.
proof_obligations.finite_contradiction: The Theorem 4.5 RHS is O_p(N^-1/4 sqrt(log N)+N^-1/8)->0, while the estimator error converges in probability to -1.
proof_obligations.growth_conditions: K=N^(1/4)=o(N^20), K->infinity, and both anchor dimensions equal N->infinity.
proof_obligations.normality_contradiction: All four Theorem 4.6 side conditions hold, but its standardized statistic equals -sqrt(K)/sigma*(1+o_p(1))->-infinity.
